newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Fraser grants itself a year to improve.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Fraser grants itself a year to improve.

text.p: Struggling British department store chain House of Fraser saw annual profits hit by restructuring charges on Thursday and executives set a one-year deadline for improvements.

The chain, floated in 1994 by the Fayed brothers who continue to own London's landmark Harrods store, said pretax profits for the year ending January 25 were 14.8 million pounds ($24 million) before exceptional charges of 53.2 million, compared with profits of 14.3 million the previous year.

"It will be precisely in one year's time that we will know (whether changes have brought improvements). That may well be the time for the swords to come out," chairman Brian McGowan told a news conference.
But he added that, "There is an awful lot to go for," pointing out that every one percentage point rise in gross profit margin added an extra six million pounds of profit.
McGowan admitted that the last three years for the group "hasn't been a happy story for shareholders and I can assure you it hasn't been a happy story for me."
The group is trying to refocus on upmarket brand names and quality own-brand merchandise, with complementary standards of service.
Chief executive John Coleman said changes the group had made should mean it could "look forward to a period of sustained sales and earnings growth."
He also ruled out any more provisions.
"We are very confident that we have got sufficient (provisions) to cover the full restructuring programme," he told Reuters.
Coleman said if the provisions were not all used, "we will hand them back as exceptional credits."
The group said both own-bought and concession sales had seen growth on a same-store basis in the early weeks of the current year.

"We are quietly confident, quietly happy with our sales performance so far," Coleman said, adding that the chain's refurbished Leeds, northern England, store was seeing sales up 70 percent over a year ago.
Shares edged up half a penny to 165 pence, just off a year high of 166.5 pence by 1226 GMT.

"The board is confident that the actions taken to strategically refocus the business, including the launch of new ranges, coupled with improvements in operational efficiency and customer service, will provide a strong platform for sustained growth in the years ahead," the company said in a statement.
The chain's turnaround proposals included selling three stores and overhauling its 51 others.
Coleman said talks were underway on the disposals but no further store closures were planned.
The company said that same-store sales in the year were up 6.3 percent, with concession sales up 15.8 percent and sales of own-brand merchandise rising 2.5 percent.
House of Fraser will be introducing private label own-brand clothing for men and women in the autumn, Coleman said, which it hopes will prove successful.
Coleman said although the private label would be a minority of sales, "we might see (it) reaching as much as 25 percent of our fashion sales."
He said further cost savings were expected from a second phase of restructuring, after savings of 10 million pounds a year were secured in the first part.
"The objective of phase two is two-fold. It's to increase customer service and to save more money," Coleman said. ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
